title: Declarative Failure Domain & Recovery Contract ADR
author: Sofia Alvarez
body:
Summary

This ADR proposes a company-wide, declarative Failure Domain and Recovery Contract specification for services and model-serving endpoints. The goal is to provide machine-readable metadata that allows orchestration, clients, and edge proxies to reason about safe recovery strategies (retry, degrade, redirect, fallback model variant), prioritized routing, and emergency limits without embedding ad-hoc logic in each service.

Motivation

Problem statement:
- Incidents often require cross-cutting coordinated behavior: clients need to reduce traffic to degraded regions, runtime should switch to lower-fidelity variants, and observability needs to surface the intended recovery path. Currently these behaviors are scattered across runbooks and service code, increasing blast radius and slow manual coordination.
- Lack of a canonical schema makes automated fallback, rate shaping, and graceful degradation brittle and error-prone.

Benefits:
- Single source of truth for expected failure and recovery semantics per service/model variant.
- Enables smart routing and automated fallback orchestration in Redwood’s runtime and edge proxies.
- Makes canary and emergency rollbacks safer by encoding allowed actions and constraints.

Scope

This ADR applies to:
- Public Redwood API endpoints (hosted inference)
- Dedicated and Private runtime sidecars in customer deployments
- Internal service-to-service RPCs that participate in multi-stage request flows (e.g., prompt-telemetry enrichment, KV prefetch).

Out of scope:
- Low-level GPU scheduling policies (covered in gpu-fleet docs)
- Legacy adapters that cannot be updated at rollout (we provide compatibility shim guidance below).

Proposal

Introduce a declarative YAML/JSON schema stored with service configuration bundles and artifact metadata. Runtime components (edge proxy, request router, sidecars) and client SDKs will read and enforce the contract at request time. The contract consists of three high-level sections: identification, failure_domains, and recovery_contract.

Example (YAML):

service: text-generation-v2
version: 2026-02-10
owner: eng-serving-runtime
failure_domains:
  - name: transient-gpu-exhaustion
    severity: medium
    scope: node
    symptoms: ["queue-depth>50", "gpu-util>=95% for 30s"]
    detection_signals: ["gpu_node_health:degraded", "request_queue:latency_p95>400ms"]
  - name: region-network-partition
    severity: high
    scope: region
    symptoms: ["control-plane-unreachable", "edge-proxy-errors>=0.5%"]
    detection_signals: ["region_probe:failed", "edge_errors:rate>0.5"]

recovery_contract:
  allowed_actions_priority:
    - reduce_concurrency: {max_reduction_pct: 50, minimum_concurrency: 1}
    - fallback_model_variant: {variant: quantized-cascade-v1, expected_cost_delta: -0.45}
    - route_to_peer_region: {max_failover_latency_ms: 120}
  retry_policy:
    idempotency: best-effort
    max_retries: 2
    backoff: exponential
    max_total_retry_time_ms: 600
  degradation_profile:
    preserve_token_quality: true
    early_exit_threshold: 0.10 # allow early-exit sampling up to 10% of inputs for latency-critical routes
  observability_contract:
    required_tags: ["failure_domain", "recovery_action", "contract_version"]
    sampling_override: p100% when action in [route_to_peer_region, fallback_model_variant]

Key fields explained:
- failure_domains: Named conditions with severity and scope to allow different recovery triggers depending on blast radius.
- allowed_actions_priority: Ordered allowed recovery actions with parameterized limits to prevent unbounded fallback.
- retry_policy: Per-service guidance consistent with API idempotency class. SDKs should surface this to clients.
- observability_contract: Guarantees for telemetry emitted during recovery paths.

Runtime behavior (high level)

1) Detection: monitoring agents emit detection_signals. An aggregator maps signals to failure_domains using rules in the contract.
2) Decision: policy engine consults allowed_actions_priority and SLOs to produce a recovery_plan (deterministic ordering).
3) Execution: edge proxies and runtime routers execute bounded actions (reduce concurrency, switch model variant, route to peer region) and annotate spans/metrics with recovery_action.
4) Telemetry: observability pipeline enforces observability_contract: required tags, increased sampling, and emergency dashboards.

SLO & Safety integration

- Each service must declare the SLOs that the recovery contract is intended to protect. Example: availability p99 99.9%, p95 latency 150ms for interactive endpoints.
- The policy engine will not execute fallback actions that would violate declared minimum quality thresholds (e.g., accuracy drop > 15%) unless the action severity == high and human override present.

Operational examples

Example 1 — Transient node GPU saturation:
- Detection: node queue depth spikes >50 and gpu_node_health:degraded reported.
- Decision: reduce_concurrency up to 50% for non-critical tenant tiers, preserve dedicated capacity for premium customers.
- Execution: router applies tenant-scoped concurrency hint, emits metric recovery_action=reduce_concurrency.

Example 2 — Region-level network partition:
- Detection: region_probe:failed and control-plane-unreachable.
- Decision: route_to_peer_region allowed with max_failover_latency_ms 120; fallback_model_variant not chosen initially to avoid quality regression.
- Execution: edge proxies begin soft-failover with traffic mirroring to validate behavior.

Schema & Compatibility

- Contract stored alongside service artifacts in artifact repository (metadata/contract.yaml).
- Backwards compatibility rules:
  1) If a runtime cannot parse the contract, it should fall back to a safe default: no automatic fallback, raise an alert, mark service as "contract-unavailable" in observability.
  2) Gradual adoption: support a "compat_version" field. Older runtimes will ignore new fields.

Implementation plan

Phase 1 (Q2 2026):
- Finalize schema and publish validation tool (CLI: rwd-contract-validate).
- Implement read-only enforcement in edge proxy (no automatic actions; just make decisions and emit recommended_action metrics).
- Create emergency dashboard and SLI queries for contract violations.

Phase 2 (Q3 2026):
- Implement action executor in runtime router and sidecars with opt-in gate.
- SDKs (Python/Go/Node) expose client-level backoff/retry hints based on contract.
- Pilot with 3 services: text-generation-v2, embeddings-indexer, prompt-telemetry.

Phase 3 (Q4 2026):
- Full rollout with enforcement flags for tenant tiers and alerting playbooks.
- Onboard Dedicated and Private sidecars; provide optional customer-configurable policy overrides for Private deployments.

Rollout checklist

- [ ] Schema spec published in confluence and repo (contracts/schema/v1).
- [ ] Validation CLI available and integrated into CI for service artifact bundles.
- [ ] Observability: required tags instrumented and emergency dashboard live.
- [ ] Runtime: edge proxy emits recommended_action metrics.
- [ ] SDKs surfaced retry/backoff hints.
- [ ] Runbook updated with recovery steps and human override procedure.

Ownership & Governance

Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-policies subteam)
Secondary owners: eng-infra (edge proxy), eng-sre (monitoring & runbooks), eng-dx (SDK exposure)

SLOs for adoption:
- 90% of new services must include a validated contract metadata file by 2026-12-31.
- Contract parsing success rate in edge proxy must be >= 99.5% in Q1 2027.

Security & privacy considerations

- Contracts are metadata and must not contain secrets. Validate that uploaded contract artifacts are scanned for sensitive fields.
- Private deployments: customers can override recovery parameters; Redwood retains the right to require minimum safety bounds for enterprise SLAs.

Open questions

- How should we quantify and expose quality regressions for fallback_model_variant actions across heterogeneous models? Proposal: require a small benchmark/metric set (accuracy/RoBERTa classifier metric or human-eval sample) attached to variant metadata.
- Should clients be allowed to opt out of server-driven fallback actions entirely? Proposal: per-API call hint allow_client_opt_out: true/false (default false for critical endpoints).

Related pages

- infra-standards/service-dependency-isolation-and-runtime-feature-gating-standards (guidance on gated features and isolation)
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/slo-driven-runtime-contracts-and-rollback-playbook (rollback and decision engine design)

Appendix: CLI examples and validation output

# Validate a contract in CI
rwd-contract-validate metadata/contract.yaml

# Sample validation output (success)
PASS: schema v1.0
WARN: unknown field 'experimental_sherpa' ignored by runtime v2026-03
OK: contract accepted for artifact text-generation-v2:2026-02-10

Consequence of rejection:
- CI failure prevents artifact promotion to staging; artifact owner receives actionable lint output.

Notes

This ADR is intended to give runtime and operator teams a low-friction path to coordinate automated and manual recovery actions across Redwood’s hosted and distributed deployments. It is designed to complement, not replace, existing runbooks and incident response procedures.
